chain255_expansion.base_output_rule: Start from an exact deep copy of successful_outputs.output_chain_255. Preserve its six non-generator members byte-for-byte as JSON values. Replace only the six named generator_marker members; the replacement products are defined below.
chain255_expansion.canonical_fixture_root_rule: Let C be a deep copy of successful_outputs.output_chain_255. In the Normative Section 15 successful-output field order, replace exactly its six generator_marker values using the named constructor and the one resolved chain255 family: existing_lock, resolution_passes, selected_packages, selected_modules, applicable_requirements, then import_graph. Preserve every other value. The resulting twelve-member object C, including scalar scanned_source_ref and every scalar record_ref ledger locator, is the canonical fixture root. No wrapper surrounds C for canonical_expanded_output_bytes.
chain255_expansion.canonical_generated_plan_root_rule: The canonical generated-plan root is exactly the three-member JSON object {"expected":C,"fixture_id":"RES-S-PASS-256","input_ref":"chain_255"}, where C is the canonical fixture root. There is no class, covers, result, diagnostic, input value, media type, length prefix, path, or other wrapper member.
chain255_expansion.canonical_json_rule: Encode each selected root exactly once with the accepted Canonical JSON Erratum: NFC strings, UTF-8 key-byte order, preserved array order, compact punctuation, no BOM, no whitespace, and no newline.
chain255_expansion.existing_lock_rule: existing_lock is exactly {input_ref:null,input_sha256:null,package_decisions:[D_1,...,D_255],unreferenced_entries:[]}, where D_i is decision_rule.
chain255_expansion.generator_order: existing_lock, resolution_passes, selected_packages, selected_modules, applicable_requirements, import_graph
chain255_expansion.graph_rule: The root node is exactly {kind:'root',module:'root_app',node:'root'}. P_i is exactly {kind:'package',name:R_i.name,node:T_i,package_id:R_i.package_id,version:R_i.version}. For i in 1..254, E_i is exactly {alias:R_(i+1).name,constraint:'1.0.0',from:T_i,source_path:'packages/' + R_i.name + '/' + R_i.version + '/module.yaml#/imports/0',to:T_(i+1)}. E_255 is exactly {alias:R_1.name,constraint:'1.0.0',from:'root',source_path:'root#/imports/0',to:T_1}. import_graph is exactly {edges:[E_1,...,E_255],nodes:[root-node,P_1,...,P_255]}. Single quotes delimit literals and are not output.
chain255_expansion.independent_construction_rule: Two independent author-side constructions are required before freezing these declarations: one materialized prefix-slice object builder using the closed schema and one separately written pass-first builder with an independent canonical JSON writer. Both must produce byte-equal C and byte-equal generated-plan roots; count or digest equality alone is insufficient.
chain255_expansion.index_rule: records are indexed 1 through 255 in ledger order; array references use zero-based index
chain255_expansion.name_rule: chain plus exactly three zero-padded decimal digits from 001 through 255
chain255_expansion.pass_rule: For p in 1..255, pass p is exactly {active_requirements:[Q_1,...,Q_p],changes:{R_p.name:{from:null,to:R_p.package_id}},input_selection:[S_1,...,S_(p-1)],output_selection:[S_1,...,S_p],pass:p,selection_decisions:[D_1,...,D_p],unchanged:false}; for p=1 input_selection is []. Pass 256 is exactly {active_requirements:[Q_1,...,Q_255],changes:{},input_selection:[S_1,...,S_255],output_selection:[S_1,...,S_255],pass:256,selection_decisions:[D_1,...,D_255],unchanged:true}. resolution_passes is the array of passes 1 through 256 in numeric order.
chain255_expansion.record_projection_rule: selection_rule and selected_module_rule are exhaustive for every selected-package and selected-module member. No ledger member is implicitly copied, omitted, renamed, reference-expanded, or added.
chain255_expansion.reference_terminal_rule: record_ref in every selection record and scanned_source_ref in C are named locator terminals, not ref:<target> expansion positions. Generated selected modules contain inline record, retained_bytes, parsed_module, and imports members and introduce no reference field.
chain255_expansion.requirement_rule: Q_1 is exactly {alias:R_1.name,constraint:'1.0.0',contributor:{kind:'root',module:'root_app'},interval:{kind:'exact',lower_inclusive:'1.0.0',upper_exclusive:null},package:R_1.name,source_path:'root#/imports/0'}. For i in 2..255, Q_i is exactly {alias:R_i.name,constraint:'1.0.0',contributor:{kind:'package',package:R_(i-1).name,package_id:R_(i-1).package_id,version:R_(i-1).version},interval:{kind:'exact',lower_inclusive:'1.0.0',upper_exclusive:null},package:R_i.name,source_path:'packages/' + R_(i-1).name + '/' + R_(i-1).version + '/module.yaml#/imports/0'}. applicable_requirements is [Q_1,...,Q_255]. Single quotes delimit literals and are not output.
chain255_expansion.selected_module_rule: Let B_i be exactly {encoding:'lowercase_hex',hex:R_i.module_hex}. M_i is exactly {imports:R_i.imports,module_file:R_i.descriptor.module_file,node:T_i,package_id:R_i.package_id,parsed_module:R_i.parsed_module,record:{descriptor:R_i.descriptor,package_id:R_i.package_id,verified_files:[{bytes:B_i,path:R_i.descriptor.module_file,sha256:R_i.module_sha256}]},retained_bytes:B_i,retained_bytes_sha256:R_i.module_sha256}; each appearance of B_i is an equal deep JSON value, not an object alias. selected_modules is [M_1,...,M_255]. Single quotes in this rule delimit string literals and are not output.
chain255_expansion.selection_rule: S_i is exactly {name:R_i.name,package_id:R_i.package_id,record_ref:L_i,version:R_i.version}. D_i is exactly {lock_entry:null,package:R_i.name,selected_by:'greatest',selected_package_id:R_i.package_id,selected_version:R_i.version,status:'no_lock_input'}. selected_packages is [S_1,...,S_255].
chain255_expansion.success_shape_rule: The stored output has all twelve successful-output members. The six generator markers expand once in generator_order. Locator terminals remain scalar strings. No generated field is recursively eligible.
chain255_expansion.symbol_rule: For i in 1..255 let R_i be family.records[i-1], let L_i be 'generated_package_families.chain255.records/' followed by the minimal unsigned decimal spelling of i-1, and let T_i be 'package:' + R_i.name + '@' + R_i.version + '#' + R_i.package_id. The plus signs denote UTF-8 string concatenation and are not output.
chain255_expansion.trailing_newline_rule: A trailing newline is outside both measured preimages and is not hashed or counted. Each measured preimage ends with the canonical JSON closing brace byte.

current_input_construction.descriptor_source_bytes: UTF-8 lines in this exact order: package: <name> LF; version: "<version>" LF; lattice: "0.3" LF; profiles: LF; each profile as two spaces, hyphen, space, value, LF in descriptor order; module_file: <path> LF; files: LF; each file as two spaces, hyphen, space, path: <path>, LF, four spaces, sha256: <digest>, LF. No other byte or child exists.
current_input_construction.package_snapshot: A readable root containing only a packages directory. Group referenced records by descriptor package, then by canonical version. packages has exactly one directory per distinct package name; each package directory has exactly one directory per referenced version; each version directory contains exact generated package.yaml and one regular file per descriptor path with exact referenced bytes. All directory child maps are exact, readable, and ordered by accepted PC6 snapshot rules; successful ScannedSource records are package-name ASCII then numeric-version order.

PC6 scan_packages over the exact portable snapshot
compare resulting ScannedSource package order, descriptors, package identities, paths, digests, and retained bytes
current_input_construction.root_source_bytes: accepted canonical JSON of exact defaulted_root, with no BOM, whitespace, or trailing newline; JSON is consumed as accepted YAML 1.2 flow source and PC4 is idempotent because all root defaults are present

reference_expansion_rule.bytes_ref: In verified_file and lock_input only, resolve once to the exact byte_constants value. verified_file consumes its decoded bytes during public PC6 package construction; lock_input consumes its decoded bytes while constructing absent, zero-byte, invalid, or parsed ExistingLockfileInput. The field is consumed and no introduced field is scanned again.
reference_expansion_rule.existing_lock.input_ref: In existing_lock_output this is lock_input_locator or null, a scalar criteria terminal. A non-null locator target is checked exactly once but the locator string remains in stored and canonical criteria.
reference_expansion_rule.existing_lock_ref: In resolve_input only, resolve a non-null value once to the exact lock_inputs object used to construct ExistingLockfileInput.
reference_expansion_rule.family_ref: In generator_marker only, resolve once to the exact generated_package_families value consumed by the named constructor. The marker and family_ref member are consumed; the constructor product is not recursively eligible.
reference_expansion_rule.future_candidate_record_refs: In non_dispatchable_future_vector.abstract_candidate_record_refs only, validate and resolve every listed package_records target once in stored order solely for the abstract future-vector ledger. The vector remains excluded from current dispatch, plans, and populations.
reference_expansion_rule.future_selected_record_ref: In future_collapse_outcome.selected_record_ref only, validate and resolve the package_records target once solely for the abstract future-vector ledger. It never enters current dispatch.
reference_expansion_rule.imports_ref: In selected_module this is module_imports_locator, a scalar criteria terminal whose unique target is checked once and whose string is not substituted.
reference_expansion_rule.input_ref: In a diagnostic or success fixture, resolve once to the exact resolve_inputs value for construction. The generated-plan metadata separately retains the original locator string as input_ref; retaining that copy is not a second reference.
reference_expansion_rule.input_refs: In a relation fixture, resolve each array element once to the exact resolve_inputs value, preserving listed order and duplicates; the stored locator array remains plan metadata.
reference_expansion_rule.package_family_ref: In scanned_source_plan only, resolve once to the exact generated family consumed by current PC6 snapshot construction; the member does not enter ScannedSource.
reference_expansion_rule.parsed_module_ref: In selected_module this is parsed_module_locator, a scalar criteria terminal whose unique target is checked once and whose string is not substituted.
reference_expansion_rule.recognition_rule: Reference role is assigned only by the closed owning schema and exact member position. A key suffix has no independent meaning. A _ref or _refs member typed as a named locator terminal is not an expansion reference; a ref:<target> expression or named reference-array item is. Unknown members are rejected by schema.
reference_expansion_rule.record_ref: In selection_record and selected_module this is package_record_locator, a scalar ledger terminal. Its unique target is checked once; it is not substituted and any fields in the target are not recursively eligible.
reference_expansion_rule.resolution_order: After strict parse and closed-schema validation: validate every locator terminal target; resolve current fixture input and output links; resolve each referenced input's existing_lock_ref, package_family_ref or package_records items, verified_file bytes_ref values, and lock_input bytes_ref; resolve each generator_marker family_ref; run the six chain constructors in successful-output field order existing_lock, resolution_passes, selected_packages, selected_modules, applicable_requirements, import_graph; form the exact canonical roots; then validate and resolve the non-dispatchable future-vector record links without dispatching them. Each applicable reference position is resolved exactly once.
reference_expansion_rule.retained_bytes_ref: In selected_module this is byte_constant_locator, a scalar criteria terminal whose unique target is checked once and whose string is not substituted.
reference_expansion_rule.scanned_source.package_records: Each package_record_ref_array item resolves once to package_records during public PC6 snapshot construction, preserving array order.
reference_expansion_rule.scanned_source_ref: In successful_output this is scanned_source_locator, a scalar criteria terminal. Its unique resolve_inputs.<name>.scanned_source target is checked once and the locator string remains in stored and canonical criteria.
reference_expansion_rule.single_expansion_rule: Resolution consumes only the original schema-typed reference position. Values or fields introduced by a target or constructor are never scanned for suffixes and are never recursively resolved. A cycle or second resolution attempt is PC7_MANIFEST_REFERENCE_INVALID at the original reference path.
reference_expansion_rule.successful_output_ref: In a success fixture, resolve once to the exact successful_outputs recipe. The generated plan stores the resulting criteria value under expected, not under successful_output_ref.
reference_expansion_rule.successful_output_refs: In a relation fixture, resolve each value once to its exact successful_outputs recipe, preserving order and duplicates; relation selectors operate on those stored recipes after any chain constructor expansion, with locator strings retained.
reference_expansion_rule.unknown_ref_key: There is no suffix-based fallback. A member not admitted by its closed schema is a schema rejection; a ref:<target> position with no unique target is PC7_MANIFEST_REFERENCE_INVALID.

compare_fields.result: Project each selector from both stored criteria operands. Every equal_fields projection must be equal and every different_fields projection must be unequal under projection_equality_rule.
compare_fields.selector_failure: Grammar, allowlist, traversal, or asserted equality/inequality failure points to the exact selector element.

retained_boundary_repeatability.comparison_representation: Each projected ordered JSON array is canonicalized and compared byte-for-byte; duplicate projected locators remain duplicate.

retained_boundary_repeatability.result: Require each resolved input host_capabilities to equal []; project each allowed selector from both stored output criteria and require ordered structural equality under projection_equality_rule.
retained_boundary_repeatability.selector_failure: A nonempty host-capability array fails at required_empty_host_capabilities; selector failures point to the selector element.

schema_language.array_rule: A named array schema supplies its item type, exact order, duplicate rule, and cross-field constraints. Generic array<T> is permitted only for recursive source JSON; it preserves source index order and permits equal values as distinct indexed values.
schema_language.constant_rule: const:true, const:false, and const:1 denote the JSON boolean or integer shown; every other const token denotes the exact UTF-8 string after the first colon
schema_language.field_selector_evaluation: Evaluation starts with the ordered one-element projection containing the operand root. '$' returns that projection. A MEMBER step replaces each projected object, in projection order, by its named member. A '[*]' step replaces each projected array, in projection order, by its elements in increasing numeric index, concatenating the results. Nested projections repeat these rules. An empty array contributes zero projected values. Duplicate values remain duplicate and keep their positions. A missing member, MEMBER on a non-object, or '[*]' on a non-array is a relation-operation failure.
schema_language.field_selector_grammar: MEMBER = [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. SELECTOR = '$' or MEMBER followed by zero or more tokens, each exactly '.' MEMBER or '[*]'. A dot always traverses an object member; '[*]' is the only bracket form. Empty segments, escapes, numeric indexes, signed indexes, quoted members, literal-dot field names, and every other bracket form are forbidden.
schema_language.identity_rule: identity:blueprint and identity:package are exact lowercase lattice:<kind>:sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal digits> strings
schema_language.integer_rule: integer excludes JSON booleans; positive and nonnegative add their mathematical bounds; pc2_json_value integers are signed i64
schema_language.map_rule: map<K,V> has unique strict-JSON string keys matching K, values matching V, non-semantic presentation order, and semantic key comparison by unsigned UTF-8 bytes

schema_language.pc2_json_value: recursive union of object with unique string keys, array, Unicode string, signed i64 integer, boolean, and null; floating and nonfinite numbers are forbidden
schema_language.projection_equality_rule: A projection is represented for comparison as one JSON array whose elements are the projected values in exact projection order. Encode that array by the accepted Canonical JSON Erratum with no trailing newline. Equality is byte equality of those canonical arrays. JSON types are distinct, object member presentation order is irrelevant, nested array order is significant, and projection multiplicity is significant; equality is never set or multiset equality.

schema_language.relation_failure_rule: After schema and reference admission, invalid selector grammar, a selector outside its operation's exact allowlist, missing-member or wrong-container traversal, wrong operand cardinality, or a false relation assertion yields PC7_MANIFEST_RELATION_OPERATION_INVALID. A selector failure or false selector assertion uses the JSON Pointer to that selector string in the stored fixture operation. A kind failure or canonical-byte mismatch uses the operation kind pointer. A cardinality failure uses successful_output_refs or input_refs as applicable. Other operation-member assertions use their exact member pointer. If several failures exist, the least pointer under the runner path rule wins.
schema_language.schema_union_rule: exactly one named variant must match
schema_language.source_path_index_erasure: For compare_after_source_path_erasure only, make a comparison copy of each operand. Recursively visit objects in unsigned UTF-8 member key order and arrays in increasing index; traversal order cannot change the result. When and only when a member name is exactly source_path and its value is a string, split that canonical Resolve path at its single '#' byte into the preserved path prefix and an RFC-6901 pointer. Split the pointer on '/' and decode ~0 and ~1. For each decoded token exactly equal to imports whose immediately next decoded token matches 0|[1-9][0-9]*, replace only the corresponding raw decimal token by '*'. Do not rescan the replacement and rejoin the untouched raw tokens with '/'. Preserve every other byte, including package-name digits, version digits, non-import pointer indexes, array positions, numbers, and strings under other member names. The comparison copy is not a Resolve output.
